name: kube-context-guard
title: Kube Context Guard
description: kubectl/helm field that shows the context, cluster and namespace a command will really use, flags production, the default namespace, a manifest namespace that disagrees with -n and a switched context, and asks for the context name before production changes.

meta.stops: Helps prevent kubectl apply on the wrong cluster
meta.summary: Shows the cluster, context and namespace a kubectl or helm command will really hit, before it runs, so production isn't changed by accident.
meta.server: Restrict production with RBAC and admission control; never rely on a client-side prompt.
catches: Production contexts, read word by word so pre-prod and nonprod aren't
Manifest namespace that disagrees with -n (helm splits it silently)
Context switched since the last command
Fixes such as adding a server-side dry run
limits: Works from the contexts you pass; it doesn't read your kubeconfig
Command parsing covers common kubectl/helm forms, not every flag or plugin
Typing the context name is friction, not authorization
a11y: Command and confirmation inputs have visible labels
Command is described by the target readback and the issues
Status uses role=status; warnings are text with aria-hidden icons
Focus returns to a nearby fix or the input after a fix
